facts.fact: A wind-felled juniper lies about ten paces downslope of the Rope-Hut door, just past the rope's eight-span reach from the sill; Meera burns its wet deadfall by day and saves the dry stick bundle for nights.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires her to drag Rohan to the door to reach the deadfall.

facts.fact: Asha's crew leaves a bundle hung in the deadfall juniper: sattu, dried apricots, a twist of salt and a strip of smoked goat, tied in the three-nested-loop knot that matches the cairn carving. Meera sketches it in the count and does not eat or decide its purpose yet.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Asha's crew leave a tied-off food cache whose knot plants clue C12.

facts.fact: Rohan takes a second half-pinch of redbark at first light this chapter; his fever has broken but he cannot walk.
facts.why: needed to bridge ch 11's fever to a lucid but weak Rohan.

facts.fact: The second man Rohan hanged was Ketan, seventeen, carrying forty pounds of salt to his mother in a high village; the first was an unnamed lowland runner of about thirty-one who carried powder for the regent's men. Rohan paid the mother's fine for the lean-to afterwards.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires Rohan to describe the boy he hanged.

facts.fact: The Shilak post's file on the guides records only the high price of a crossing, not the double rate for the rich or the free crossings for the poor. Rohan has read it eleven times.
facts.why: needed to support Rohan's line that the double price is in no record.
